content.title: Arizona defeats Purdue to earn Final Four berth: Live updates and reaction from NCAA Tournament Elite Eight game
content.text: The Wildcats trailed at halftime but dominated the second half to clinch a spot in Indianapolis for the Final FourArizona is headed to the Final Four for the first time since 1997. Getty ImagesShoutout TNT Sports analyst Jim Jackson, who succintly summed up what this Arizona team is like — and what they showed in the second half:💬 “Arizona is like AI. They gather data. It modifies their gameplan. And then they become deadly. It’s their adaptability.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementLeBron chimes inLeBron James, whose son Bryce is redshirting on Arizona but still with the team, is lending his support to the Wildcats:Burries heats up late Getty Images Arizona’s frontcourt powered its dominant second half, but Brayden Burries slammed the door. Burries heated up from the 3-point line and added six rebounds and three steals, including one that set up an Ivan Kharchenkov breakaway dunk to essentially seal it. Arizona’s other star freshman with a big contribution tonight.Brutal finish to sterling career Associated PressTrey Kaufman-Renn played a crucial role in Purdue’s turnaround from a shocking upset in 2023 as a No. 1 seed to making the national title game in 2024, and he has remained a crucial part of the Boilermakers in the two seasons since. A rough way to end a phenomenal tenure in West Lafayette, as Kaufman-Renn went 5-for-14 and dealt with foul trouble to finish with just 10 points.Purdue set to reload Getty ImagesMatt Painter's recruiting class coming in next season has an uncanny resemblance to the skillsets of his three core departing seniors. Luke Ertel is a 6-foot-1 guard who’s a former quarterback with passing vision and a nice 3-point shot. Jacob Webber is a 6-6 knockdown shooter who can shoot it off screens (similar to Loyer) and shoot from deep.Sinan Huan is a 7-foot big man who’s raw but has some natural touch and mobility.Rivers Knight is a 6-8 stretch forward. Could they be the core of the next great Purdue era? Antoine West Jr. also redshirted this season and is a former four-star prospect.Wildcats too strong, too deep Associated PressArizona's balance is just so impressive. Jimmy Jackson mentioned it on the broadcast several times tonight: The Wildcats have so many weapons that it is hard to focus on one or two players.We saw that throughout this game. Arizona finished with four players scoring in double figures, led by Koa Peat with 20. Ivan Kharchenkov added 18, while Jaden Bradley and Brayden Burries each had 14.Purdue just could not handle them all.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementLoyer: 'You gotta experience failure' Getty Images Fletcher Loyer after the game: 💬 “You gotta experience failure.” The trio of Purdue seniors — Loyer, Braden Smith and Trey Kaufman-Renn — didn't leave after going through adversity, particularly in the tournament. And the players felt they were better for it.Purdue made the national championship, but also experienced heartbreak, losing in the Round of 64 in 2023 and the Sweet 16 in 2022 to two Cinderella programs in Fairleigh Dickinson and Saint Peter’s. Arizona’s size ultimately was too much to overcome for Purdue, the preseason No. 1 team.How Arizona got over the hump Associated PressAs Arizona finally snaps a 25-year Final Four drought, it’s fitting that one of the most anticipated freshman recruits to ever come out of the state was the one leading the way.Lindsay Schnell has more on the night Koa Peat etched his name into Wildcat lore forever.Rough finish for Kaufman-Renn Getty ImagesTrey Kaufman-Renn never seemed to get into a rhythm in this game for Purdue. Maybe it was the early foul trouble with two in the first half, but he only picked up one more foul the rest of the way. The Boilermakers' best offensive player on the inside finished with 10 points on 5-of-14 shooting and two rebounds. That's a tough way to end a career.Arizona dominates second half Getty ImagesIt's hard to believe, but about an hour ago or so, it felt like this was going to be a good finish. But after trailing by seven points at halftime, Arizona completely dominated the second half. The Wildcats outscored the Boilermakers 48-26 in the second half.It's going to be hard for anyone to beat this team.What a career Getty ImagesBraden Smith finished tonight with 13 points, five rebounds and seven assists. That assist total adds to his NCAA record. More important than all the impressive stats, Smith won a lot of games at Purdue. College basketball will miss him next season. SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementKharchenkov also clutchIvan Kharchenkov, Peat’s fellow freshman and frontcourt partner, was also excellent around the rim — especially in the second half. Not only did he have 18 points — nearly all of which came in the paint — but he added some stifling defense and even a steal on the other end.Watching Peat and Kharchenkov up against Yaxel Lendeborg in the Final Four (if Michigan wins tomorrow) would sure be someything...The moment Arizona wonYour browser does not support the video tag.Here’s what it looked like in San Jose the moment Arizona returned to the Final Four for the first time in 25 years, courtesy of our Matthew Ho.One more note on Peat Associated PressEarlier, Lindsay Schnell mentioned how she felt like Koa Peat has an NFL-caliber body. She’s not too far off. Koa’s older brother, Andrus Peat, is an NFL offensive lineman for the Pittsburgh Steelers.Oh yeah, Peat also won four straight state championships at the high school level.That Final Four hat does not fit on Koa Peat's head.Readers' thoughts on Arizona's win Getty ImagesAdam F.: Everyone at halftime who said Purdue is better than us and that they’re just better, I cautioned let’s just see the second half, we came out made adjustments, and the better team showed itselfJacob R.: The way Tommy Lloyd made such a dramatic change at half with his adjustments just makes me realize how much I hope he doesn’t go to UNC.Sal M.: What happened to this Purdue team in the second half? Did they leave their guts in the locker room?Jon D.: I have enjoyed watching Smith, Loyer, and TKR all these years. Sad to see them end their careers this way.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementPeat on getting Arizona back to the Final FourAnd let’s hear from Koa Peat...💬 “I’m just proud of the guys. We kept fighting. We fought through adversity. We played teams like that. We played in the Big 12, so we were ready for the challenge. We faced adversity — all glory to God.“Just being a kid from Arizona taking this team to a Final Four, it’s a blessing. I’m proud of these guys. We worked for this. We’re not done yet. Bear Down.”Peat was superb Getty ImagesFour years ago, I traveled out to Perry High School in Gilbert, Ariz., to report on a guard named Cody Williams, who had just led his team to a state championship along with a star freshman forward who everyone in Arizona high school basketball circles was raving about. I focused on Williams because his older brother, Jalen, was about to get drafted into the NBA by the Oklahoma City Thunder (which is going pretty well for him). Cody Williams turned out well, getting drafted by the Utah Jazz after one season at Colorado. But I wish I had spent more time around that freshman forward, because as a college freshman, he just led Arizona to a Final Four.Koa Peat was vital for the Wildcats tonight — a game-high 20 points on 9-of-18 shooting, stepping up and using his size and athleticism as his fellow Arizona big men adjusted to Purdue’s strong paint defense. Peat helped keep Arizona in it in the first half, then was crucial in the Wildcats’ dominant second half. Getty ImagesTommy Lloyd quickly realizes his TV interview is being shown inside the arena in San Jose and turns to the crowd:💬 “What I’m most happy for is these Arizona fans. You guys deserve this! I know this — there’s a good-looking guy with white hair looking down on us right now, and he’s happy.”The first name of late legendary Arizona coach Lute Olson is quickly shouted back from the Wildcats fans in attendance. 💬 “We had a little bad stretch at the end of the first half, (but) these guys, winning’s in their DNA. Like I always say, they’re way better players than I am a coach, and I’m just so proud of them. ... We’re gritty. And if we’re not gritty, we’re the word that rhymes with gritty.”Can Arizona bring a natty back to the west? Getty ImagesNo team west of Waco has won a national championship since 1997. Arizona may fix that. When it is on a roll, I don't think anyone can beat Arizona. Just a complete basketball team that can win in so many ways.
